title: Who Is Rekha?
logline: Inside the marriage bureau the groom stops the chooda coming off, buys his way into the gang and photographs Mausi's ledger with keys Kiran steals from her hip; then Billu puts the photograph from the groom's pocket on Mausi's desk, and Mausi recognises the scar she dressed herself.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; Mausi, Didi, Damaad ji, Jijaji, beta, lakh and chooda kept as spoken in India.
script_note: Indian English in Latin script. Spoken text equals subtitle text once the square-bracket tags are removed.

characters.name: Kiran
characters.role: LEAD. The bureau's vanishing bride. Walked in at dawn with the groom who caught her, as his partner in crime. The scar in his photograph is under her left chooda.
characters.look: Indian woman, 27, about 5 ft 3, slight and wiry. Oval face, wheat-brown skin, straight dark brows, large kajal-lined eyes, closed watchful mouth. Black hair, centre parting with a thin line of red sindoor, low bun at the nape, two loose strands at the temples (in b5 Mausi re-pins the same bun). Small round red bindi, thin plain gold ring in the LEFT nostril, small gold ear studs, short black-bead mangalsutra. Period 2: plain ash-grey cotton salwar-kurta, knee-length, round neck, three-quarter sleeves ending a hand's width above the chooda; grey salwar; plain grey dupatta over the left shoulder; flat black sandals. Red-and-ivory chooda on BOTH forearms, read as a red cuff about 10 cm long with a pale band at each end. Block henna on both hands: one solid disc in each palm, every fingertip dipped to the first joint, backs plain. The left cuff covers the scar in every frame of this episode; no frame shows the scar.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, late 20s, alto with a dry edge. Indian English of a small-city Madhya Pradesh woman who learnt it at school and from a phone, with a light Hindi accent: simple, quick, contractions. Keeps Mausi and Didi. With Aditya: low, flat, quick, short sentences. With Mausi she sounds younger. With Chhoti: Didi's voice, tired and protective. Under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill; true things come after a pause. Not British, not American.

characters.name: Aditya
characters.role: The groom, a pharmacist, playing a thief who married a thief so that Mausi lets him in. He wants her ledger in police hands, and the owner of the scarred hand for himself.
characters.look: Indian man, 33, about 6 ft, tall and narrow, slight stoop. Long clean-shaven face, light-brown skin, calm deep-set eyes, thin mouth, short neat black hair with a left side parting, rimless rectangular glasses in every shot. Plain cream cotton-silk wedding kurta, band collar, three cloth buttons, sleeves folded back once, creased after the night and the drive; side pocket on the right holds the creased photograph (until Billu lifts it in b2) and the paper fold (all episode). Cream churidar, tan sandals. Brass key about 5 cm long on a doubled red cotton thread, outside the kurta at mid-chest, in every shot. Plain steel watch, brown strap, left wrist, never readable. Phone: plain grey.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, early 30s, light baritone, soft-spoken. Careful Indian English of a small-city Madhya Pradesh science graduate, with a light Hindi accent: complete sentences, precise nouns (dose, police, proof, page, investment), no slang. Even and unhurried, almost courteous. Playing the generous husband for Mausi, he is no louder. Under pressure he slows down and drops in volume; he never shouts. Not British, not American.

characters.name: Shakun Mausi
characters.role: Owner of Shubh Lagan Marriage Bureau and Beauty Parlour. Runs the brides; the only mother Kiran has had.
characters.look: Indian woman, 56, about 5 ft 2, broad and heavy-shouldered, sits like she owns the chair. Round face, brown skin, heavy-lidded shrewd eyes, wide mouth with paan-reddened lips, a smile that arrives before she speaks. Large round maroon bindi, small gold nose stud, grey-streaked black hair oiled into a tight bun. Starched bottle-green cotton saree with a narrow mustard border, pallu pinned on the left shoulder, plain mustard blouse with elbow sleeves, thin gold chain, rubber slippers. A dozen plain green glass bangles on each wrist. A steel ring of about eight keys hooked into the saree at her LEFT hip until Kiran lifts it at the end of b5; from b6 on her hip is bare.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, mid 50s, low, warm and grainy, a paan-chewer's unhurried mouth. Warm, motherly Indian English with a strong Bundelkhand Hindi accent, short plain sentences; Hindi endearments kept (beta, Damaad ji). She sounds like someone's aunt at a wedding. Laughs easily. Never raises her voice: the colder the thought, the softer and slower she gets. Fully voiced and clear in every line, never a whisper, including the last two lines of the episode. Not British, not American.

characters.name: Billu
characters.role: Mausi's driver, lookout and the bride's 'brother'. Calls every groom Jijaji. Lifts the photograph from the groom's pocket.
characters.look: Indian man, 30, about 5 ft 7, wiry and restless. Brown skin, sharp jaw, patchy stubble, quick eyes, black hair gelled straight back. Faded blue denim jacket with the sleeves pushed up over a black round-neck T-shirt, dark jeans, white sneakers gone grey. Wooden toothpick in the right corner of his mouth; car key on a plain steel ring hooked on his right index finger. In b7 his forearms are wet from washing the car. No weapon.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, about 30, light tenor, fast, a little nasal, talks round a toothpick. Quick, slangy small-town Indian English with a heavy Bundelkhand Hindi accent, an article dropped now and then; keeps Jijaji and Mausi; 'girlfriend' said as a street joke. Cocky and joking when he thinks he is in charge; to Mausi quick and obedient. Never American street slang, not British.

characters.name: Chhoti
characters.role: The next bride in training, three months at the bureau. Her first wedding is tomorrow (day 3).
characters.look: Adult woman, 19, about 5 ft 1, slight, wide curious eyes, light-brown skin (D-007 direction 14: she reads as an adult woman; no child's markers, no ribbon). One long black braid pulled forward over her right shoulder. Plain mustard-yellow cotton kurta with short sleeves, white salwar, a plain dupatta, rubber slippers. Two thin green glass bangles on the right wrist; left wrist bare; both forearms plainly unmarked. Henna half finished, block style: the LEFT palm has its solid disc and dipped fingertips, the RIGHT hand is still bare. A phone in a plain pink cover always in her right hand.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, 19, a young woman's voice, not a child's: bright, quick, sing-song, a giggle in the breath. Light, eager small-town Indian English with a Hindi accent, short sentences, the Indian question tag 'no?'. Keeps Didi. When frightened the voice goes small and the giggle goes. Not British, not American.

location: Shubh Lagan Marriage Bureau and Beauty Parlour, a ground-floor shop behind a grey roll-down steel shutter, shut to customers. Front room: pink walls; mirror wall on the left with a row of bare bulbs and two black parlour chairs; a shelf of unlabelled bottles; in the corner a shop mannequin with a smooth featureless face in a red bridal lehenga and dupatta; Mausi's wooden desk and chair at the back facing the shutter, a grey steel cashbox on the desk; a low wooden cot with a folded quilt along the right wall. Behind the desk a curtain of plastic marigolds leads to the back room: a steel trunk of bridal sarees, a rail of blouses, a floor mat, a small wall mirror, a back door to an alley. No readable text anywhere in the image; the shop name and ledger rows are overlays.
time_of_day: Day 2, morning, about 5:45 to 9:00 am. Shutter up, daylight from the front, tube light on. b1 to b4: low early sun, long pale light across the floor. From b5 on: high, flat, brighter morning light; the change of light marks the passing morning (D-007 advisory). No clock overlay.

beats.action: Opens on the hands, inside the last moment of s1a01, at Mausi's desk. Shot 1 (insert, silent): Mausi's fingers in their green glass bangles hold the first ivory bangle of the LEFT chooda at Kiran's knuckles; Kiran's fingers are straight. Shot 2 (insert, under l01): the same hands, Kiran's left hand now a fist so the bangle cannot pass; Aditya's long hand, steel watch on his wrist, laid over Mausi's. Shot 3 (insert, under l02 and l30): folded notes put down on the desk beside the grey cashbox. Shot 4 (Mausi single, under l03): she laughs, paan-red smile. Shot 5 (insert, tail of l03): Kiran's right hand pushes the ivory bangle back up into place; the left cuff is whole again and stays whole for the rest of the episode. Near miss 3: he stops it himself, to sell the husband and buy his place.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Leave it on, Mausi. It suits my bride.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Get Chhoti a new set instead.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] And this, my first investment in the business.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [laughs] Our Damaad ji has a big heart!

beats.action: He is in. Shot 1 (two-shot, under l04): Billu hugs Aditya, grinning over his shoulder, toothpick in the right corner of his mouth, car key on his right index finger. Shot 2 (insert, from the tail of l04 into the gap): two of Billu's fingers lift the white edge of the creased print out of the side pocket on Aditya's right; only the print, the paper fold stays in the pocket. Shot 3 (Mausi single at the desk, under l05): one key unhooked from the ring at her left hip, the cashbox open, she writes in a thick ledger bound in red cloth. Silent after: Shot 4 (insert): the cashbox lid shut and locked, the key back on the steel ring at her left hip. Shot 5 (Aditya single): his eyes down on her hip. Billu now has the photograph; the viewer knows where the proof is kept and where its key hangs.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [laughs] Jijaji! You're one of us now.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] I've written your money in the book, Damaad ji. Now you're a partner too.

beats.action: At the mirror wall, each speaking to the other's reflection, low, while Mausi works at her desk out of frame. One face per frame; the mirror wall stays out of wides (D-007 direction 16). Set-up A: Aditya's reflected face in the mirror, bare bulbs along the frame edge, the back of Kiran's bun soft in the foreground (l06). Set-up B: Kiran's reflected face, his cream shoulder and the red thread soft at the frame edge (l07). Set-up A2, closer on his reflection (l08, l09). Set-up B2, closer on hers; she finishes his sentence (l10). Her left forearm, cuff whole, rests in her lap below the frame line.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] Where is Rekha?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Mausi's accounts first. Rekha isn't going anywhere.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] You said Rekha keeps the accounts. Here, Mausi keeps them.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] And if it's a lie, then—

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [flatly] Then eleven days, then one dose. I remember.

beats.action: Back room, behind the marigold curtain: Chhoti and Kiran sit side by side on the steel trunk among folded bridal sarees. Aditya is in the front room with Mausi, not in any frame. Shot 1 (two-shot, l11): Chhoti holds her pink phone out to Kiran in her right hand, screen turned away from camera: tomorrow's groom. Shot 2 (Kiran single, l12). Shot 3 (Chhoti single, l13): the giggle drops for a moment. Shot 4 (Kiran single, l14). Shot 5 (insert, l15): Chhoti's hennaed LEFT fingertips touch the red cuff on Kiran's left forearm. Shot 6 (insert, l16): Kiran's right hand lifts Chhoti's hand off the cuff and puts it back in Chhoti's lap. Silent after: Shot 7 (Chhoti single), surprised, then the smile again. Near miss 4: Kiran stops her, and he is not in the room.

lines.speaker: chhoti
lines.text: [excited] Didi, look! I marry him tomorrow. Smart in the photo, no?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [flatly] Yes. In the photo.

lines.speaker: chhoti
lines.text: [nervous] It's only one night, isn't it?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Yes. One night.

lines.speaker: chhoti
lines.text: [laughs] You've done nine weddings, Didi! Can I try on the chooda?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [sharply] Don't wear this, Chhoti.

beats.action: Later; the light is now high and bright. Front room. Mausi in her chair at the desk; Kiran on the floor sideways to the chair, her right shoulder against Mausi's left knee, so the steel key ring at Mausi's LEFT hip hangs just above Kiran's right hand. Shot 1 (two-shot, l17): Mausi's hands, oil on the fingers, re-pinning Kiran's low bun, as she has since Kiran was a girl. Shot 2 (Kiran single, l18): eyes down. Shot 3 (Mausi single, l19): smiling, hands still in Kiran's hair. Silent after: Shot 4 (insert): Kiran's right hand, henna disc on the palm, at Mausi's hip, fingers round the key ring. Shot 5 (insert): Kiran's right fist closed round the keys in her lap beside her left cuff; above the frame Mausi's hands are still in her hair. She steals from the hands that are mothering her.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] It was me who named you Kiran. Remember?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] I remember, Mausi.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Next week I'll put the eighteen lakh in your hand myself.

beats.action: Silent before: Shot 1: Mausi's back, a red wedding blouse over her arm, going through the marigold curtain to fit Chhoti; her LEFT hip bare: no key ring. Then: Shot 2 (insert, under l29): behind the mannequin's red dupatta, Kiran's right hand presses the key ring into Aditya's palm. Shot 3 (under l20): Kiran standing in the gap of the curtain with her back to the front room and the camera, Mausi's voice from behind it; Mausi and Chhoti are not seen. Shot 4 (insert, under l21): the cashbox lid up, Aditya's hands lifting the red cloth ledger. Shot 5 (insert, under l22): his grey phone held over an open ledger page, rows of parties and advances (overlay text), his thumb stopped on one row. Shot 6 (Aditya single, under l23): close and low, the glow of a reply on his screen lit in his glasses (reply text as an overlay, in support only). Shot 7 (insert, under l24 and l31): the cashbox locked; behind Kiran's back his hand puts the key ring back into her right hand, and her fingers close over it. Mausi's line about tomorrow's groom plays over the thumb on the row. Timing flag for S7 (D-024): shot 7 now carries about 9.9 s of lines (l24 then l31); hold it on its camera move, or let l24 begin over the tail of shot 6.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [whispers] Mausi's keys. The book's in the cashbox.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [laughs] Chhoti, breathe in! It's a blouse, not a sack.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] Mausi, what's tomorrow's boy like?

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] A simple boy, beta. He agreed quickly.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] Kiran, I've photographed every page. The proof has reached the police in my town.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] They've told the nearest police post. The police will be here in half an hour.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [sighs] Till then, Mausi mustn't find out.

beats.action: Mausi is back at her desk. Kiran and Aditya are across the room by the mannequin near the shutter, out of earshot and out of this frame. Silent before: Billu comes in from the shutter, forearms wet from washing the car for tomorrow. Two-shot (Mausi seated, Billu leaning over the desk): he lays the creased print face up in front of her (l25) and grins, sure it is a joke about the groom's old girlfriend (l26). He speaks low, to her only.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [chuckles] Mausi, this was in Jijaji's pocket.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [laughs] Looks like some old girlfriend's hand!

beats.action: No line. Three set-ups. Shot 1 (insert, about 3 s): the print in Mausi's green-bangled fingers, the one approved photograph image (story_locks.photograph): a young man's hand palm up, a veiled bride's left hand on it, red glass bangles at the wrist, the pale crescent on the outer forearm, a temple step. Shot 2 (Mausi close, about 2 s): the smile stays exactly where it was; her eyes have dropped to the left of frame. Shot 3 (insert, about 2 s): Kiran's left hand at her side by the mannequin, the red cuff whole on the forearm, the grey sleeve above it. Mausi knows the crescent at once: she dressed it. The temple step and the glass bangles tell her which wedding, and so which boy.

Shot 1 (Mausi single, Billu soft behind her shoulder, under l27): Kiran and Aditya have crossed from the mannequin to the front of the desk at her look; she lifts the print toward Aditya, warm as ever, his cream shoulder and red thread at the frame edge. Shot 2 (Mausi single, closer, under l28): she has turned her face to Kiran; gently. Silent after: Shot 3 (insert): behind Kiran's back, her left hand with its red cuff slides out of sight; her right fist holds the stolen key ring. Shot 4 (Aditya single, glasses, key on its red thread): his eyes on Kiran, having gone from the print to Mausi to her. Cut to black on his look.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Damaad ji... are you looking for this hand?

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Shall I tell him, beta? Whose hand this is?

sfx_notes: Bed, whole episode, loopable (the series' one bureau ambience): tube-light hum, a slow ceiling fan, a thin distant morning street through the open shutter (a cycle bell, a far scooter). No crowd voices and no customers anywhere. The back room in b4 is the same bed, deadened and closer.
b1: a soft click of the ivory bangle against the knuckles at the open; paper of the folded notes on wood under l02; the bangle settling back into the cuff under the tail of l03.
b2: denim rustle of the hug; one small chink as Mausi unhooks a single key; pen scratch on ledger paper under l05; cashbox lid and lock clack, then the key's chink back on the ring at her hip.
b3: a faint buzz from the bare mirror bulbs over the room tone.
b4: silk sarees shifting on the trunk; a tiny tick of glass as Chhoti's fingertips meet the cuff under l15.
b5: hairpins, a comb, oil on fingers. The keys do NOT chink when Kiran takes them: her hand closes round the ring. The missing chink is the point; keep the bed even under it.

b6: plastic marigold curtain rustle as Mausi goes through; l20 and l22 come from behind the curtain, slightly duller but fully voiced and clear. Cashbox key, lid. No camera-shutter sound from Aditya's phone. l29 is the episode's one whisper, behind the mannequin; keep the bed even under it. One short phone vibration for the reply at the end of l23, before l24, so the reply answers the pages he has just sent. Cashbox lock under l24. l31 sits on the room tone, nothing over it.
b7: grey sneakers on the floor; a drip from Billu's wet hands on the desk as he lays the print down.
b8: the room tone thins (fan and street drop away); only the tube-light hum and one held low music note.
b9: duck the bed and music right down under l27 and l28 so every word is clear; Mausi is fully voiced, never whispered. After l28, silence, one low sting on the cut to black.
music_note: The series' small theme set, used sparingly. b1 to b7: no score, or the thinnest pulse under b6's ledger shots only. b8: one held low note enters as Mausi looks at the print. b9: it ducks under both of Mausi's lines and resolves into a single low sting on the cut. Nothing sweet under b5; the scene plays on the room.
ending_question: Will Mausi hand her girl's secret to the son-in-law or shield her, and what will Aditya do before the police arrive in half an hour?
writer_notes: English adaptation (S5) of script.hi.json after its D-024 clarity pass (26 Nov), not a literal translation. The pre-pass English file is script.en.prev.json. Same beats b1 to b9, same line ids (l01 to l31), same speakers and order, same emotion tags in the same positions, same silent_seconds, silent_position, heard_as, action, on_screen, sfx_notes and music_note as the Hindi file. Only text, target_seconds, names, voice_note, title, the language fields, ending_question, these notes and the English figures in clarity_pass differ.

Byte-identical to script.en.prev.json (text, tags and targets), so their English takes in voice/takes.en.json stay valid: l01, l02, l03, l04, l06, l07, l08, l09, l10, l12, l13, l14, l16, l17, l18, l19, l20, l21, l22, l25, l27, l28. These are the lines the Hindi pass kept unchanged. Of them only l01 is quoted in docs/clarity-cold-viewers.md (cv_A s1a02 item 1), and the fault there is the missing reason, not the wording; new l30 carries the reason, as in the Hindi, so l01 stays. l20, l21 and l22 gain heard_as off_screen, mirroring the Hindi; their text is unchanged.
Reworded to mirror the Hindi: l05, l11, l15, l23, l24, l26. Added: l29, l30, l31. Re-voice in English: those nine lines only.

Glosses English needs and Hindi does not: chowki is said in plain English, 'the nearest police post' (l24), the ledger glossary carrier for this term on path A; s1a03 b10's place super 'Police post' relies on it. 'Advance', 'setting' and 'in-charge' are gone from English as from Hindi. No thana, SI, SHO, FIR, malkhana, bureau or tola is spoken in this episode, so none needs a gloss here. Chooda was glossed in English in s1a01 l07 (ledger). Mausi, Didi, Damaad ji, Jijaji and beta are forms of address the cast use throughout and are kept, as before.

One word per object: 'the book' is the physical red account book (l05, l29), matching s1a03 en l12 ('Take the book too'); 'accounts' stays the word for हिसाब (l07, l08). 'Proof' (l23) echoes s1e01 en l17 ('The police want proof').

Register: l30 and l23 keep Aditya's complete, precise sentences (investment, photographed, proof). l05 keeps Mausi's short warm sentences with Damaad ji; 'partner' renders हिस्सेदार. l11 'I marry him tomorrow' is Chhoti's quick present tense, and sets up l21's 'tomorrow's boy'. l26 is Billu's street joke; it says 'hand' once so that Mausi's 'this hand' in l27 points at something heard. l31 'Till then' is Indian English for तब तक.

Timing: spoken targets total 110.6 s, plus 24 speaker changes at 0.3 s (7.2 s), plus silences of 20.2 s (unchanged) = 138.0 s. Targets for unchanged lines are kept as they were. New and reworded lines are sized at about 11 to 12 characters a second, the rate the existing English takes ran at. The projection that counts is clarity_pass.projected_finished_seconds.

Against the Hindi targets, new and reworded lines: l05 6.3 against 6.4, l11 5.0 against 5.2, l15 4.8 against 5.0, l23 7.0 against 7.0, l24 6.8 against 6.8, l30 4.0 against 4.4, l31 3.0 against 2.8. Two run about 11 to 13 per cent short: l26 (3.4 against 3.8) and l29 (4.0 against 4.6, a whisper, which may run slower in the take). All are inside 15 per cent. b6 shot 7 carries l24 and l31, about 9.8 s of English targets: the same S7 flag as the Hindi (hold the move, or start l24 over the tail of shot 6).

Tags: all Hindi tags kept, including the change on l24 from [calm] to [quietly] (Mausi is behind the curtain). l29 is the one whispered line in the episode; l23 and l24 are [quietly], not whispered, so there are no three whispers in a row. [flatly] (l10, l12) is in the verify-in-casting group; if the Kiran voice ignores it, swap to [calm]. The take notes warn that Kiran's short English [quietly] lines can come out whispered (l14, l18); l31 is tagged [sighs], not [quietly], for that reason. Short turns that may need extra takes: l06, l09 (cut-off), l12, l14, l18.

Pronunciation dictionary candidates for the English voices: Mausi (MAU-see), Damaad ji (da-MAAD jee), Jijaji (JEE-jaa-jee), beta (BAY-taa), Didi (DEE-dee), Chhoti (CHHO-tee), chooda (CHOO-daa), lakh (laakh, not 'lack'), Rekha (RAY-khaa), Kiran (KI-run).

Faces per frame: two at most in every shot (D-007 direction 16); b3 is one face per frame and the mirror wall stays out of wides. on_screen lists everyone visible across the beat's shots, not in one frame. In b6 Mausi is seen once, from behind, in shot 1, her left hip bare (no key ring); after that she is voice only. There is no crowd: the bureau is shut to customers.

The last spoken line (l28) asks the question and does not answer it. ending_question is worded differently: what Mausi will do with what she knows, and what Aditya will do, with the police half an hour out.

This file has not been run through a JSON parser (the S5 session had no shell); it was written by hand with no backslashes or double quotes inside strings. Line ids, beat ids, order, speakers, heard_as and tags were checked against script.hi.json by eye, not by a tool.

As in the Hindi: l21 plays over shot 4, an insert of Aditya's hands at the cashbox; Kiran is not in that frame.

fixes.fault: cv_A s1a02 (1): 'Why does Aditya want the chooda left on?' New 'And this, my first investment in the business.' over the notes in shot 3 makes him the generous husband buying his way in. l01 and l02 untouched.
cv_A s1a02 (2): 'Your money's down as advance. Advance for what?' Now 'I've written your money in the book, Damaad ji. Now you're a partner too.' Names 'the book' for l29 and s1a03 l12.
'Tomorrow's groom' pointed at a phone screen turned away from camera. Now 'I marry him tomorrow', which also sets up l21.
'nine' had no noun; now 'nine weddings'. Incidental number, said once.
The key theft (b5) and the cashbox (b2) were pictures only. Kiran says, over the hand-off in shot 2, 'Mausi's keys. The book's in the cashbox.' Nothing about the hand.

cv_A s1a02 (3): 'Who is he saying this to?' l23 names his listener (Kiran), says what the phone picture shows (every page photographed) and that the proof reached the police in his town, paying off s1e01 l17.
'the police post here' with no chain, and chowki is a word English needs glossed. Now 'They've told the nearest police post. The police will be here in half an hour.' Tag [quietly].
